/* ============================================================
   GOLD LAYER — FACT TABLE
   Olist E-Commerce Analytics Project

   Purpose: builds fact_order_items, the central fact table of
   the star schema. Grain: one row per order line item (i.e. per
   product within an order — an order with 3 different products
   produces 3 rows here). Each row links out to every dimension
   via its surrogate key, and carries the numeric measures
   (price, freight, payment total, average review score).

   Must be run AFTER the dimension script, since this table
   joins against dim_customer, dim_product, dim_seller and
   dim_date to look up their surrogate keys.
   ============================================================ */

-- Database context is set by the pipeline's linked service (DBName = db_olist_gold);
-- uncomment the line below if running this script standalone in Synapse Studio.
-- USE db_olist_gold;

/* ------------------------------------------------------------
   Idempotent drop, same pattern as the dimension script: only
   drop if it exists (DROP EXTERNAL TABLE doesn't support
   IF EXISTS directly), so this script can be safely re-run by
   the automated pipeline.
   ------------------------------------------------------------ */
IF EXISTS (SELECT * FROM sys.external_tables WHERE name = 'fact_order_items')
    EXEC('DROP EXTERNAL TABLE fact_order_items');

CREATE EXTERNAL TABLE fact_order_items
WITH (LOCATION = 'fact_order_items/', DATA_SOURCE = gold_lake, FILE_FORMAT = parquet_ff)
AS
SELECT
    -- Surrogate key for the fact table itself, ordered by the natural
    -- grain (order_id + order_item_id) so it's deterministic on every rebuild.
    ROW_NUMBER() OVER (ORDER BY oi.order_id, oi.order_item_id) AS order_item_key,

    -- Foreign keys: translate each natural business key into its
    -- dimension's surrogate key via a join, rather than storing the
    -- natural key directly — keeps the fact table lean and consistent
    -- with standard Kimball star-schema design.
    dc.customer_key,
    dp.product_key,
    ds.seller_key,
    dd.date_key AS order_date_key,

    -- Degenerate dimensions / natural keys kept for traceability
    oi.order_id,
    oi.order_item_id,

    -- Measures
    oi.price,
    oi.freight_value,
    pay.total_payment_value,
    rev.avg_review_score

FROM OPENROWSET(BULK 'olist_order_items_dataset', DATA_SOURCE = 'silver_lake', FORMAT = 'DELTA') AS oi

-- Orders table brought in purely to get customer_id and the purchase
-- timestamp — order_items itself doesn't carry those.
JOIN OPENROWSET(BULK 'olist_orders_dataset', DATA_SOURCE = 'silver_lake', FORMAT = 'DELTA') AS o
    ON oi.order_id = o.order_id

-- Dimension lookups (INNER JOIN — every order item should have a
-- valid customer/product/seller/date; a row silently disappearing
-- here would indicate a data quality issue worth investigating).
JOIN dim_customer dc ON o.customer_id = dc.customer_id
JOIN dim_product dp ON oi.product_id = dp.product_id
JOIN dim_seller ds ON oi.seller_id = ds.seller_id
JOIN dim_date dd ON CAST(o.order_purchase_timestamp AS DATE) = dd.Date

-- Payments: a single order can have multiple payment rows (e.g. split
-- across installments or payment methods), so we pre-aggregate to one
-- row per order_id BEFORE joining — otherwise the join would fan out
-- and duplicate every order_item row per payment record, silently
-- inflating price/freight totals downstream.
LEFT JOIN (
    SELECT order_id, SUM(payment_value) AS total_payment_value
    FROM OPENROWSET(BULK 'olist_order_payments_dataset', DATA_SOURCE = 'silver_lake', FORMAT = 'DELTA') AS p
    GROUP BY order_id
) pay ON oi.order_id = pay.order_id

-- Reviews: same fan-out concern as payments, plus TRY_CAST instead of
-- CAST — a single malformed/non-numeric review_score value would
-- otherwise fail the entire CETAS statement; TRY_CAST just returns
-- NULL for that one bad value instead, which AVG() then ignores.
LEFT JOIN (
    SELECT order_id, AVG(TRY_CAST(review_score AS FLOAT)) AS avg_review_score
    FROM OPENROWSET(BULK 'olist_order_reviews_dataset', DATA_SOURCE = 'silver_lake', FORMAT = 'DELTA') AS r
    GROUP BY order_id
) rev ON oi.order_id = rev.order_id;
